nodes.title: note: sort_by
widgets_values: area assumes your target person is largest tracked object (it will get blue), else use left_to_right. generally though the model does OK even if subject isn't the blue mask, better if it is

nodes.title: replacement_mode
widgets_values:
bool isn't absolute. Mask inputs and prompt seem to be MUCH more important. the 
Scail2 team says "Without a correct mask Animation mode collapse into Replacement-Mode behavior in certain inputs."

nodes.title: IMAGE INPUT NOTES
widgets_values:
The mask is a critical input to SCAIL-2 even in Animation Mode. To visualize the channels that the mask is actually for, we encode them with colors:

POST SAM:
Black — tells the model the background at this location should not be visible.
White — tells the model the background at this location should be visible.
Color — encodes the correspondence between character regions and the driving motion.

ANIMATION MODE: 
Place the character on a BLACK background if you are just showing character and don't want any background used. Don't do a white background

Toggle the 'replacement_mode', false will copy the motion and animate the character in the character's background
WanScailToVideo

nodes.title: NOTES ON MASKS
widgets_values:
In the driving video, using animation mode, anything that is colored will either come through to the output as is OR the model will fill in that area based on what it thinks it should in the prompt.

If there is a person and dog, and the conditioning prompt is 'person, dog' in SAM3.

The mask (assuming max_objects high enough) should show both color shadows.

In the SCAIL prompt you can put "A person is walking their pet dragon, it has a scale tail and horns" and it will replace dog with dragon. Or you could say they are walking dog and the original dog should come through especially if you describe it
